body.statement:
For every finite-rational, finite-discrete ordinary full-kernel instance \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{ord}}\in\mathfrak D_{\mathrm{AEK}}\), every ordinary full-kernel identifying collection \(\mathbf B\) yields an accepted physical batch certificate \(E_{\mathbf B}\) with shared-protocol cost
\[
 \sum_{S\in\mathcal P(E_{\mathbf B})}\sum_{a\in S}c(a)
 =\sum_{B\in\{B_i\}_{\mathrm{distinct}}}\sum_{v\in B}\kappa_v.
\]
Conversely, every accepted batch certificate in \(\iota(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{ord}})\) yields, after adding zero-cost READ actions and coalescing equal RAND-endpoint sets, an ordinary full-kernel identifying collection of no greater cost.  Hence batch feasibility agrees in both representations and
\[
 \operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{batch}}=\operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{ord}}.
\]
With source laws and support tables provided by the stated oracle and all returned bits charged to \(N_{\mathcal O}\), the published NP-hardness and \((1-o(1))\ln|V|\) inapproximability threshold, unless \(\mathrm{NP}\) has quasi-polynomial-time algorithms, transfer oracle-relatively to this SELECT--RAND--READ batch image.  No batch-to-scalar reduction, standard explicit-input hardness claim, or approximation for the general physical catalogue is asserted.
body.justification: The theorem gives a typed two-way cost map for the published all-cells kernel only through an explicit shared-charge batch.
body.gap: A full kernel is not one scalar query, and opaque law replies prevent an unqualified bit-complexity transfer.
body.consumer: Ordinary hardness calibrates the explicit SELECT--RAND--READ batch image.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{ord}}\in\mathfrak D_{\mathrm{AEK}}\).  For \(B\subseteq V\), Definition~\(\mathrm{Ordinary\ full\mbox{-}kernel\ design\ embedding}\) gives
\[
 S_B=\{s\}\cup\{r_v:v\in B\}\cup\{\rho_v:v\in V\}.
 \tag{25}
\]
It has one fresh-unit SELECT, executes every mechanism at most once, respects precedence, has no conflicting pair, and satisfies the stipulated ordinary CTF-REALIZE condition.  Thus \(S_B\in\Pi\).  Independence and uniformity of the RAND coordinates imply, for every \(b\in\mathfrak X_B\),
\[
 \Pr\{R_B=b\}=\prod_{v\in B}|\mathfrak X_v|^{-1}>0.
 \tag{26}
\]
The slice and label definitions then give
\[
 \operatorname{Slice}(S_B,\ell_{B,b})
 =P_b(V\setminus B)=Q[V\setminus B](\cdot;b).
 \tag{27}
\]
All vertices are READ, so measured ancestry holds.

Let \(\mathbf B\) be ordinary full-kernel identifying.  Its target contains every \((x,s)\), and its source family contains every \((B,b)\) in (27).  Lemma~\(\mathrm{Single\mbox{-}world\ operational\ specialization}\) makes the complete translated run return nonfailure for every target cell.  Applying Theorem~\(\mathrm{Sparse\ switching\ source\ normal\ form}\) separately to each cell produces \(E_{\mathrm{sw}}^{x,s}\).  Use the shared protocol set \(\mathcal P_{\mathbf B}=\{S_B:B\in\{B_i\}_{\mathrm{distinct}}\}\), as required by the batch definition.  By (26), every actually used label event is positive.  The zero SELECT and READ costs and (25) yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \sum_{S\in\mathcal P_{\mathbf B}}\sum_{a\in S}c(a)
 &=\sum_{B\in\{B_i\}_{\mathrm{distinct}}}\sum_{v\in B}c(r_v)\\
 &=\sum_{B\in\{B_i\}_{\mathrm{distinct}}}\sum_{v\in B}\kappa_v.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{28}
\]
Hence the forward batch is accepted and has exactly the ordinary shared acquisition cost.

Conversely, let \(E_{\mathrm{batch}}=(\mathcal P,(E_{\mathrm{sw}}^{x,s})_{x,s})\) be accepted in the embedded catalogue.  For \(S\in\mathcal P\), put \(B(S)=\{v:r_v\in S\}\).  Adding every missing zero-cost READ preserves SELECT cardinality, mechanism use, precedence, conflicts, physical compatibility, and cost.  Coalesce protocols with the same \(B(S)\) and call the resulting ordinary collection \(\mathbf B(E_{\mathrm{batch}})\).

It remains to show that every source slice used by a component certificate is available from the corresponding full ordinary family.  Suppose its label fixes RAND coordinates \(D\subseteq B(S)\) at \(b_D\), leaves the remaining RAND coordinates unconditioned, and conditions on a READ event \(R=r\).  For every recorded event \(A\), independence and uniformity give
\[
 \Pr_S(A\mid R_D=b_D,R=r)
 =\frac{
 \displaystyle\sum_{b_{B(S)\setminus D}}
 \left(\prod_{v\in B(S)\setminus D}|\mathfrak X_v|^{-1}\right)
 P_{(b_D,b_{B(S)\setminus D})}(A,R=r)}{
 \displaystyle\sum_{b_{B(S)\setminus D}}
 \left(\prod_{v\in B(S)\setminus D}|\mathfrak X_v|^{-1}\right)
 P_{(b_D,b_{B(S)\setminus D})}(R=r)}.
 \tag{29}
\]
The denominator is positive because this conditioning event is actually used by an accepted record.  Formula (29) is a finite rational operation on members of \(\mathcal Q_{\mathbf B(E_{\mathrm{batch}})}\).  It invokes no positivity for an unasserted READ cell.  Therefore every used source and marginal factor is in the permitted deterministic preprocessing closure of that ordinary family.  Applying the single-world specialization lemma to each accepted component proves ordinary operational acceptance for every cell \((x,s)\), so \(\mathbf B(E_{\mathrm{batch}})\) is full-kernel identifying.

Coalescing and the zero SELECT and READ costs give
\[
 \sum_{B\in\mathbf B(E_{\mathrm{batch}})}\sum_{v\in B}\kappa_v
 \leq\sum_{S\in\mathcal P}\sum_{a\in S}c(a).
 \tag{30}
\]
Taking infima in (28) gives \(\operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{batch}}\leq\operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{ord}}\), and taking infima in (30) gives the reverse inequality.  The same maps prove equality of feasibility, hence
\[
 \operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{batch}}=\operatorname{Opt}_{\mathrm{ord}}.
 \tag{31}
\]

The cited Akbari--Etesami--Kiyavash theorem gives a polynomial reduction from minimum-weight hitting set to their ordinary minimum-cost full-kernel intervention problem, and their cited corollary gives the \((1-o(1))\ln|V|\) threshold under the stated quasi-polynomial-time assumption.  Their displayed construction uses prohibitive auxiliary costs.  On a finite rational weighted instance with total original weight \(W\) and \(N\) vertices in the constructed graph, replace each prohibitive cost by the integer
\[
 C_{\mathrm{aux}}=(N+1)(W+1).
 \tag{32}
\]
An original hitting set has cost at most \(W\), so an exact optimum never selects an auxiliary vertex.  Any approximation with ratio below \(\ln N\leq N\) also has output cost less than \(NW<C_{\mathrm{aux}}\) and therefore cannot select one.  The binary encoding length of (32) is polynomial in the weighted input length.  Binary observed domains may be assigned because the reduction's identification obstructions are graphical.  Thus the cited hardness statements persist on the finite-rational, finite-discrete ordinary class.

Finally, (28)--(31) are cost-preserving reductions between that class and the batch SELECT--RAND--READ image.  The structural catalogue is polynomially written, but its complete law and support replies can be exponential and are supplied by \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{src}}\).  Consequently the transfer is relative to that oracle convention, with all returned bits charged to \(N_{\mathcal O}\); it is not a standard explicit-input NP-hardness assertion.  Because the construction concerns a finite batch and only SELECT--RAND--READ actions, it gives neither a batch-to-scalar reduction nor an approximation result for the general physical catalogue.
